subject: pclxs D9 divergence: \$_ identity — a bound global is a copy, not an alias
description: Later in the week. Under perl, `\$_` inside a block IS the caller's SV; under pclxs the binding is published/read-back, so identity is lost — a block that compares refaddr, or stashes \$_ and writes through it later, diverges. Asserted against perl in t/89-gvsv.t (the `identity=captured` case) so it cannot change quietly. Copying cannot fix it: it needs a host that can genuinely alias a variable to a value it is handed, at which point D9 becomes a capability group like `io` with the copy path as fallback. Open question to answer first: does anything in a real closure actually rely on it? Nothing measured so far does.
